record.original_question: Define (and detect) the quantum Chern class. 7.2 Inverse problem for quantum integrable systems (commun icated by A. Pelayo and S. V u Ngo. c) The notion of quantum integrable system as a maximal set of commut ing quantum observables is fairly well established now. It is a very old notion, going back to Bohr, Somm erfeld and Einstein [71] in the early days of quantum mechanics. Nonetheless the theory didn't blo ssom at that time because of the lack of technical tools needed to solve interesting problems about q uantum integrable systems. For recent surveys discussing the spectral geometry of integrable s ystems, see [188, 181]. The most elementary results about the symplectic structure of cla ssical integrable systems, such as the existence of action-angle variable, did not fit well in Schr odinge r's quantum setting at that time because they involve the analysis of differential and pseudodifferen tial operators, only developed since the 1960s. This is a prominent part of analysis and PDE (the most mat hematical side of quantum mechanics), that goes by the name of "microlocal analysis". The microlocal analysis of action-angle variables starts with the pion eering works of Duistermaat [67] and Colin de Verdi` ere [51, 52], and was followed by many other authors (see [49] for further references). For compact symplectic manifolds, the study of quantum action-an gle variables is very recent, it goes back to Charles [48], using the theory of Toeplitz operators. Toeplit z operators give rise to a semiclas- sical algebra of operators with symbolic calculus and microlocalization properties, isomorphic (at a microlocal level) to the algebra of pseudodifferential operators (s ee Boutet de Monvel-Guillemin [42]). The classification of semitoric systems in [185, 186] (see Section 1) g oes a long way to answering the fascinating question "can one hear the shape of a semitoric system "? More precisely, the idea is to recover the classical semitoric invariants from the joint spectrum of a quantum integrable system, as much as possible.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a compact connected symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$, and let $F=(F_1,\dots,F_n):M\to\mathbb{R}^n$ be a smooth map whose components Poisson-commute, $\{F_i,F_j\}=0$, and which is a momentum map for an effective Hamiltonian action of $\mathbb{T}^n$ on $M$ (so $(M,\omega,F)$ is a symplectic-toric manifold). In this case the Delzant polytope $\Delta=F(M)\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ together with the integer affine structure inherited from $\mathbb{Z}^n$ determines, via its outward primitive normal vectors at each facet, characteristic classes of $M$, in particular the Chern classes $c_k(TM)\in H^{2k}(M;\mathbb{Z})$.

A quantization of $(M,\omega,F)$ is given by a self-adjoint semiclassical operator family $(\hat F_{1,\hbar},\dots,\hat F_{n,\hbar})$, $\hbar\in(0,\hbar_0]$, of Berezin–Toeplitz (or pseudodifferential) type, acting on a family of Hilbert spaces $\mathcal H_\hbar$, such that $[\hat F_{i,\hbar},\hat F_{j,\hbar}]=0$ and the principal symbols are $F_1,\dots,F_n$. The joint spectrum 
$$\Sigma_\hbar=\operatorname{JointSpec}(\hat F_{1,\hbar},\dots,\hat F_{n,\hbar})\subset\mathbb{R}^n$$
is, modulo $O(\hbar^\infty)$, an $\hbar$-dependent discrete subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$.

Problem. Provide an intrinsic definition of a "quantum Chern class" attached to such a quantum integrable system, characterized by the following requirements:

(a) (Definition) For each $k\in\{0,1,\dots,n\}$ define an invariant $c_k^{\mathrm{q}}(\hat F_\hbar)$ of the quantum integrable system $(\hat F_{1,\hbar},\dots,\hat F_{n,\hbar})$, depending only on its unitary equivalence class up to $O(\hbar^\infty)$.

(b) (Semiclassical limit) Show that, in the semiclassical limit $\hbar\to 0$, the invariant $c_k^{\mathrm{q}}(\hat F_\hbar)$ recovers the classical Chern class $c_k(TM)\in H^{2k}(M;\mathbb{Z})$ of the underlying symplectic-toric (or, more generally, semitoric) manifold.

(c) (Detection) Give an explicit constructive procedure that recovers $c_k^{\mathrm{q}}(\hat F_\hbar)$ from the asymptotics of the joint spectrum $\Sigma_\hbar$ as $\hbar\to 0$ alone, without knowing the operators $\hat F_{i,\hbar}$ a priori.

Carry this out in the toric setting, and extend the construction to the semitoric setting in dimension $4$ (where $n=2$ and one component $F_1$ generates an effective $S^1$-action while singularities may include focus-focus points).
artifact.status_search_result: A literature search does not return any work explicitly defining or detecting a "quantum Chern class" for quantum integrable systems. Related work by Pelayo, Vũ Ngọc, Le Floch and others has constructively recovered classical symplectic invariants of semitoric systems from joint semiclassical spectra, but the specific question of defining and spectrally detecting a quantum analogue of the Chern class appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The inverse spectral problem for quantum semitoric systems
status_evidence.snippet: Explicit formulas recover, from the semiclassical asymptotics of the joint spectrum, all symplectic invariants of the underlying classical semitoric system.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work spectrally detects classical semitoric invariants but does not address a quantum Chern class.

status_evidence.title: San Vu Ngoc - One can hear semitoric systems
status_evidence.snippet: Inverse problem for quantum semitoric systems; recovery of symplectic invariants from joint spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: The author's program addresses inverse spectral problems but no published definition of a quantum Chern class is reported.
